mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes thermal equilibrium?

options.A: No net flow of heat between two systems in contact

mcqs.answer: No net flow of heat between two systems in contact
mcqs.explanation: Thermal equilibrium is reached when two systems in contact exchange no net heat; their temperatures become equal. Options B, C and D describe unrelated properties.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate zeroth law to temperature measurement
mcqs.question: How does the zeroth law enable temperature measurement?

options.A: It defines temperature as a property that determines the direction of heat flow
options.B: It states that if two bodies are each in thermal equilibrium with a third body, they have the same temperature, allowing the third body to serve as a thermometer
options.C: It directly relates temperature to the internal energy of a system
options.D: It provides a formula for converting between temperature scales

mcqs.answer: It states that if two bodies are each in thermal equilibrium with a third body, they have the same temperature, allowing the third body to serve as a thermometer
mcqs.explanation: The zeroth law tells us that a system (the thermometer) in thermal equilibrium with another system shares its temperature, so the thermometer can reliably indicate that temperature. Options A, C and D are not the basis for temperature measurement.

mcqs.question: The zeroth law of thermodynamics states that

options.A: Energy cannot be created or destroyed
options.B: The entropy of an isolated system never decreases
options.C: If two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other
options.D: Heat spontaneously flows from a colder body to a hotter body

mcqs.answer: If two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other
mcqs.explanation: This is the precise statement of the zeroth law. Option A describes the first law, B the second law, and D is opposite to the actual direction of spontaneous heat flow.

mcqs.question: Two metal blocks A and B are placed in contact with a third block C. After some time no heat flows between any of the blocks. Which statement is true?

options.A: Block A is hotter than block B
options.B: Block B is hotter than block C
options.C: All three blocks are at the same temperature
options.D: Block C is at a lower temperature than block A

mcqs.answer: All three blocks are at the same temperature
mcqs.explanation: When no heat flows between any pair, each pair is in thermal equilibrium, implying equal temperatures for A, B and C by the zeroth law. The other options contradict the observed lack of heat flow.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate zeroth law to temperature measurement
mcqs.question: A mercury thermometer placed in a beaker of water stabilizes at a certain height. Which principle explains why the thermometer reading equals the water temperature?
mcqs.explanation: The thermometer (system C) reaches thermal equilibrium with the water (system A); by the zeroth law they share the same temperature, so the reading is the water temperature. The other laws address energy conservation, entropy, or gas behavior, not temperature equivalence.

mcqs.question: A scientist uses a calibrated thermocouple (system C) to compare temperatures of two unknown samples A and B. The thermocouple shows no voltage difference when connected to A, and also none when connected to B. What can be concluded?

options.A: Sample A is hotter than sample B
options.B: Sample B is hotter than sample A
options.C: Samples A and B are at the same temperature

mcqs.answer: Samples A and B are at the same temperature
mcqs.explanation: No voltage indicates the thermocouple is in thermal equilibrium with each sample. By the zeroth law, if both are in equilibrium with the same reference (C), they must be at the same temperature. Options A and B contradict the observation; D is unnecessary because the same zero reading occurs for both samples.

mcqs.question: A common misconception is that thermal equilibrium means the objects are not exchanging any energy at all. Which statement correctly clarifies this?

options.A: In thermal equilibrium, objects may exchange heat continuously but the net heat flow is zero
options.B: No microscopic collisions occur between particles in thermal equilibrium
options.C: Objects must be isolated from each other to achieve thermal equilibrium
options.D: Their temperatures are different but balanced

mcqs.answer: In thermal equilibrium, objects may exchange heat continuously but the net heat flow is zero
mcqs.explanation: Thermal equilibrium implies equal temperatures, so any microscopic heat exchange averages out to zero net flow. Options B and C are false; D contradicts the definition of equilibrium.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate zeroth law to temperature measurement
mcqs.question: If a thermometer (system C) reads 25°C when placed in contact with system A, and also reads 25°C when placed in contact with system B, what can be inferred about the temperatures of A and B?

options.A: A and B must both be at 25°C, because the thermometer is in thermal equilibrium with each, as stated by the zeroth law
options.B: The thermometer could be faulty, so no conclusion can be drawn
options.C: A and B could have different temperatures, but the thermometer averages them
options.D: The reading only tells that A and B are both hotter than the thermometer

mcqs.answer: A and B must both be at 25°C, because the thermometer is in thermal equilibrium with each, as stated by the zeroth law
mcqs.explanation: Since the same calibrated thermometer reaches thermal equilibrium with both systems and shows the same temperature, the zeroth law tells us the two systems share that temperature. Options B, C, and D ignore the implication of equilibrium with a reliable thermometer.
